title: Impeachment court on 'leeway' for defense: Admit evidence first, exclude later if needed
summary: Responding to the observed “leeway” given to the defense panel during Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial on Thursday, the Impeachment Court explained that it is better to admit evidence…

blocks.text: Responding to the observed “leeway” given to the defense panel during Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Thursday, the Impeachment Court explained that it is better to admit evidence first, as it can simply be excluded later should concerns arise.

“If there is doubt on whether to admit or not admit any evidence such as testimonial evidence, it is better for the judge to admit it. So that if he considers it in error afterwards, then he can just give it no probative value at the time that he will make a decision,” impeachment court spokesperson Atty. Regie Tongol said.

On Day 44 of Duterte’s impeachment trial, one of the objections raised against the defense panel was its presentation of a money laundering expert as a witness. The prosecution argued that the vice president is not facing any money laundering charges.

“The witness is apparently delivering his credentials on anti-money laundering but the respondent in this case is not being charged with money laundering crimes,” House prosecutor and Akbayan Rep. Chel Diokno said.

“The issue before this court are all centered on unexplained wealth, non-declaration of SALN, and participation in business. And I haven’t heard anything from this witness that would qualify him on those matters,” he added.
While initially allowing the defense to continue its questioning, Senator and presiding officer Chiz Escudero would later agree with Diokno, issuing a clarification.

“The chair has given you enough leeway on this aspect but I have to cite and state that the Honorable Diokno is correct. AMLC or violation of the AMLC is not per se, part of the charge in Article II,” Escudero said.
According to Tongol, Escudero was merely adhering to the policy that presiding officers should be liberal in receiving evidence.
He noted that Escudero was simply extending the same liberality to the defense as he did during the prosecution panel’s presentation of evidence.

During the trial, other objections raised were the defense’s presentation of a video clip during the impeachment trial of late Chief Justice Renato Corona and a defense witness’s capability to testify on a report “he had not read.” —LDF, GMA News
